sec: Causes of hypothyroidism and clinical features

items.q: Match the following causes of hypothyroidism to the source's grouping — 1) Iatrogenic 2) Drug-induced 3) Iodine-related 4) Autoimmune/other … A) Post-thyroidectomy / post-radioiodine B) Lithium, amiodarone, interferon-α, immune checkpoint inhibitors C) Iodine deficiency / excess D) Hashimoto thyroiditis, infiltrative disease
items.exp: The page clusters iatrogenic (post-surgery, post-RAI), drugs (lithium, amiodarone, IFN-α, ICIs), iodine (deficiency or excess), and autoimmune/other causes (Hashimoto, infiltrative). (Book p905)

items.q: A bipolar patient on lithium develops overt hypothyroidism one year after starting therapy. Which mechanism best fits the source?
opts: Lithium increases TSH receptor antibody binding
items.exp: Lithium inhibits thyroid-hormone release and can also cause goitre; the page lists it under drug-induced hypothyroidism. (Book p905)

items.q: Assess these drug-induced statements: I Interferon-α can cause irreversible hypothyroidism. II Amiodarone causes hypothyroidism only via the Wolff-Chaikoff effect.
items.exp: IFN-α's thyroid effects are usually reversible after stopping; amiodarone causes hypothyroidism by multiple mechanisms, not only Wolff-Chaikoff. (Book p905)

items.q: Which is the odd one out — a drug not on the source's hypothyroid list?
items.exp: Lithium, amiodarone and IFN-α are listed as causes of hypothyroidism; propranolol only treats thyrotoxic symptoms. (Book p905)

items.q: The single most common worldwide cause of hypothyroidism on this page is ___.
items.exp: Iodine deficiency is the global leader; in iodine-replete countries Hashimoto dominates. The page explicitly calls out iodine deficiency first. (Book p905)

items.q: Match the following endocrine disorder to its expected thyroid phenotype on the page — 1) Bipolar disorder on lithium 2) Patient receiving IFN-α for hepatitis C 3) Patient receiving amiodarone 4) Newborn in iodine-deficient region … A) Acquired hypothyroidism B) Often reversible thyroiditis C) Can cause hypo- or hyperthyroidism (Type 1 vs 2) D) Endemic cretinism
items.exp: Lithium causes acquired hypothyroidism; IFN-α usually produces reversible thyroiditis; amiodarone can produce either Type 1 or Type 2 patterns; severe iodine deficiency causes endemic cretinism. (Book p905)

items.q: A patient on amiodarone develops overt hypothyroidism; uptake scan shows high iodine uptake with elevated IL-6. Which amiodarone type is most consistent?
items.exp: Type 2 amiodarone thyrotoxicosis is destructive thyroiditis with low uptake and high IL-6; hypothyroidism with high uptake and raised IL-6 sits in the destructive pattern. (Book p905)

items.q: Assess amiodarone: I It can produce both hypothyroidism and thyrotoxicosis. II Type 1 is a destructive thyroiditis.
items.exp: Amiodarone causes both hypothyroidism and thyrotoxicosis; Type 1 is iodine-induced hyperthyroidism, Type 2 is destructive thyroiditis. (Book p905)

items.q: Match the following clinical feature of hypothyroidism to its system — 1) Cold intolerance, weight gain 2) Bradycardia, pericardial effusion 3) Menorrhagia, galactorrhoea 4) Carpal tunnel syndrome … A) Constitutional B) Cardiovascular C) Reproductive D) Musculoskeletal / neurological
items.exp: Cold intolerance and weight gain are constitutional; bradycardia and pericardial effusion are cardiovascular; menorrhagia and galactorrhoea are reproductive; carpal tunnel syndrome is musculoskeletal/neurological. (Book p905)

items.q: A 45-year-old woman presents with weight gain, cold intolerance and menorrhagia. The least likely coexisting finding on this page is:
items.exp: Exophthalmos is a feature of Graves thyrotoxicosis, not hypothyroidism; carpal tunnel, bradycardia and hypercholesterolaemia all appear in the hypothyroid features list. (Book p905)

items.q: On the source's clinical-feature diagram, the least common but most pathognomonic neuropsychiatric feature of severe hypothyroidism is ___.
items.exp: Hashimoto encephalopathy is the rare but pathognomonic CNS complication; the other items are common but not pathognomonic. (Book p905)

items.q: Evaluate hypothyroidism clinical features: I Pleural and pericardial effusions occur. II Obstructive sleep apnoea is associated.
items.exp: The page lists pleural and pericardial effusions plus obstructive sleep apnoea among hypothyroid features. (Book p905)

items.q: Which is the odd one out among causes of primary hypothyroidism listed on the page?
items.exp: Secondary (central) hypothyroidism is not a primary thyroid failure and is grouped separately; the other three are primary gland failure. (Book p905)
